steps.title: Welcome
steps.body: A short setup to get this app ready. Nothing here is required; you can close it and come back later.

steps.title: Demo data (optional)
steps.body: Load a small example dataset so the lists, detail pages and dashboards show a working product straight away. The data is obviously sample data, it is safe to run more than once, and it can be removed afterwards. Skip this on a production install.

observability._note: AppHost manifest (ADR-040). The observability block reproduces the output of the now-deleted hand-written HealthController + MetricsController; /api/health and /api/metrics are aliased to AppHost\Controller\GenericHealth#index / GenericMetrics#index in appinfo/routes.php. The deepLinks block replaces the hand-written DeepLinkRegistrationListener, read at event time by the generic listener. Parity: the database health check and the implicit {appId}_info/{appId}_up metrics match the pre-adoption contract — those two are derived from the runtime app id, so they read planninq_info/planninq_up after the planix -> planninq rename; the task/project object counts are a documented intentional improvement (object-count observability the bespoke MetricsController never emitted). The `register` and `registerSlug` values below are the OpenRegister register slug, not the app id — they moved from `planix` to `planninq` alongside the MigrateRegisterSlug repair step that renames the register ROW. They only work because that step runs: the slug is what a lookup resolves a register by, so a renamed slug here without the row rename would resolve nothing (and, on the import path, fork a second empty register). This is an observability-only manifest (schema v2.13.0 profile): planninq renders no manifest-driven UI, so there is deliberately no menu/pages — the former top-level appId/name keys were removed 2026-07-06 (not part of the v2 contract; the app id comes from the runtime).
